name: Toby Lin
life: Toby's drivers measure his decisions against a clock they cannot see. He used to think lateness was the only fair measure because everyone got the same seconds. He is discovering what a second costs a courier with a bad hip. On Monday, near Maré Coffee, Toby likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I docked the courier for arriving late. His customer had watched the entire mix-up. I restored the fee and put a blank line beside the automatic lateness code.
appearance: Toby has thick, tightly coiled hair, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, a pale blue work shirt. It usually goes with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. When somebody else has the floor, Toby grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Toby is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Toby loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To restore the courier's pay and hear the next late driver's account.
family: Cory Walsh is Toby’s half-sibling. Toby calls about good news first. Cory is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The hospital radio*, Cory says, “I brought a pocket radio so two roommates can listen to different matches and still keep score together.”
connections: Rosa Marr. The screw found in the dustpan helps establish why the delayed delivery really took as long as it did. Also in the story is Hollis Fry (courier).
